This analysis considers the newly refined drag coefficients provided by Sandia National Laboratories based on CFD analysis. The proposed design consists of 4 stud link chain shots of 40 mm diameter and 500m length, with Stevpris Mk5 drag anchors. 7.2 External Mooring System The MTV design will allow connection to a preexisting mooring system by 4 connection points, one in each corner of the vessel. The preexisting mooring will mostly consist of catenary lines with surface buoys to which the vessel would attach, as seen in Figure 7-3. The detailed design of this mooring system will be largely dependent on the deployment site, so it will have to be designed case by case. This mooring system will primarily be used in deeper sites (>50 m). One of the options would be to use a 4-point mooring system, as seen in Figure 7-3. Final Technical Report 29/57 Figure 7-3 Four-point external mooring system representation To demonstrate the compatibility of the vessel with an external mooring system, a preliminary design has been developed for a potential deployment site off the coast of Florida. This mooring system is also based on a catenary mooring system but in a single-point mooring configuration, as it was proposed by FAU based on their experience with mooring platforms on the site. The vessel is moored with two ropes (i.e., polyester lines), one from each hull, that come together at an intermediate node (bridle configuration) to continue as a single rope to a surface buoy permanently installed on site. This surface buoy is connected to the seabed by a catenary using a stud link chain and a drag anchor. In the following figure, a schematic of the configuration is shown.
